This produces a posterior distribution that corrects for the market's systematic bias toward the favorite. The derived kernel, the 'Bayesian Spine', maps directly to GSI's thesis-scoring framework by providing a well-calibrated uncertainty quantile for each side of the spread. Its breakdown regime occurs when environmental variables (like extreme air density) violate the linearity assumption in the logistic regression table, leading to overconfident predictions.
